To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phonology of syllables in Bengalese song depends upon the syllables that precede or follow it in the sequence, and that premotor activity in RA is modulated in a manner consistent with this sequence-dependence of syllable phonology.
syllable phonology varies significantly based on the preceding and following syllable in Bengalese song.

the acoustic structure of individual syllables in Bengalese Finch song varies depending on the sequence of preceding or following syllables, and that premotor activity in a brain region associated with syllable production is also sequence-dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms of birdsong, which is an excellent model of vocal learning and motor control.
the neural basis of vocal communication in songbirds, a group of birds that are known for their complex, learned, and stereotyped vocalizations.
how the brain controls complex, sequenced behaviors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
birdsong, like human speech, is controlled by linked representations of phonology and sequence.
the syllable phonology of birdsongs, as in human speech, is controlled by the central nervous system and is dependent on the context in which it is being produced.

the sequencing of song syllables is controlled by a network of brain regions, including the robust nucleus of arcopallium, and that the sequence of syllables in turn influences the acoustic structure of individual song syllables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the brain coordinates the production of discrete elements of behavior, such as syllables in birdsong, with their sequence into complex patterns, and that this coordination occurs at multiple stages of motor processing.
the brain coordinates the sequence and phonological properties of birdsong syllables by linking their premotor activity.
we have shown that syllables in birdsong are controlled as discrete units, but that their phonology is not independent of their sequence in the song.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sequencing and phonological structure of birdsong are controlled together, as they are in human speech.
birdsong syllables, like syllables in human speech, are not controlled independently of sequence.
the sequencing and the phonology of syllables in song are intimately related.
